clue.text: Suffering a hot bum, right? Dress in these!

indicators.note: suffering suggests something in torment and disarray, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a scorched backside is advised to put on something suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' scrambles A HOT BUM, R (right) and DRESS together; 'these' points to the garment the clue is about, the knee-length shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the item of clothing being recommended, the knee-length casual shorts named after the Atlantic island.

clue.text: Sharon's flyers name one other battle

parts.note: El Al is the Israeli national airline, Ariel Sharon having been an Israeli prime minister

indicators.note: other asks for the letters to be made into something different, a rearrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Israeli politician's airline names yet another battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel Sharon was an Israeli prime minister, hence the national airline; 'other' is an unusual anagram signal, asking for a different arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Second World War desert clash in Egypt in 1942 is one of history's best-known battles.

clue.text: Condition of many headless nodules

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A medical complaint involving a great many lumps without tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' reads as an adjective with 'headless nodules', but it is the Roman thousand on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The viral infection that swells the salivary glands is a medical condition.

clue.text: Sound measure destroyed bed lice

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thorough treatment has wiped out the lice in the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges BED LICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit for measuring the loudness of a noise is a sound measure.

clue.text: He took no bloody interest in Venice

definitions.text: He took no bloody interest in Venice

parts.words: He took no bloody interest in Venice
parts.note: the Shakespeare moneylender in Venice waived interest on his loan but demanded a bloody pound of flesh

explanation.surface: A Venetian who was indifferent to bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice the moneylender charges Antonio no interest, taking a pound of flesh as forfeit instead; 'bloody' plays on the British swear word too.
explanation.definitionFit: The moneylender in Shakespeare's play lent money interest-free but wanted flesh as his bond.

clue.text: Tars, men on stormy decks

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors work on deck in rough weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges TARS, MEN and ON; 'decks' is a verb, not the ship's floors.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to adorn it, so decks as a verb means adorns or embellishes.

clue.text: Trial hero's Irish girlfriend turning up in Siberia

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the hero of Kafka's The Trial is Josef K, so K plus S for the possessive
mot is Irish slang for a girlfriend

explanation.surface: A Kafka character's Irish sweetheart appears in Siberia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses KS + MOT. The definition means a place in Siberia.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Tom river is one of the main cities of western Siberia.

clue.text: What's French and saucy incited Americans' glee

indicators.note: incited means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Something French and risqué provoked delight among Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incited' rearranges AMERICANS and GLEE. 'saucy' is not cheeky here; it means served as a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The French custard sauce poured over desserts is literally a French thing in sauce form.

clue.text: Hot rapper rapping a choice. Hunt for one!

indicators.note: rapping suggests knocking about, so the word beside it is knocked into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the elite is the choice or pick of a group

explanation.surface: A rap artist gives a quick-fire performance of a choice track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rapping' rearranges RAPPER into PRERAP. Hunt is William Holman Hunt, a founder of the Victorian art brotherhood, not a search.
explanation.definitionFit: Holman Hunt was a member of the brotherhood of painters, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Country cousin's opening company with the goods

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom or country

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word

parts.note: Coy is the British Army abbreviation for a company

explanation.surface: A rural relative opens a firm that sells genuine products.
explanation.walkthrough: COY for company is military shorthand, as in 'A Coy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something the goods means it is the genuine article, exactly the sense of the idiom.

clue.text: Here Belgians note a partition with the French

parts.note: mur is the French word for a wall or partition

explanation.surface: Belgians record a dividing wall with their French neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a place where Belgians are found.
explanation.definitionFit: The city at the meeting of the Sambre and Meuse is in Belgium, a place where Belgians live.

clue.text: Substance of setter with solution

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
ANS is an abbreviation for answer, a solution

explanation.surface: The setter offers the essence of a puzzle along with its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Substance in the sense of wealth or resources is a person's financial wherewithal.

clue.text: This compiler going to the stake? Quite the reverse!

definitions.text: This compiler going to the stake? Quite the reverse!

parts.words: This compiler going to the stake? Quite the reverse!
parts.note: a compiler of a book of bets does not go to the stake like a martyr; the stakes come to him

explanation.surface: A crossword setter facing martyrdom by burning.
explanation.walkthrough: A compiler of the book of bets at a racecourse has stakes brought to him rather than being taken to one.
explanation.definitionFit: The bookie compiles a book of bets, and punters hand their stakes over to him.

clue.text: Don't start casual topless nooky in here: not in this condition!

indicators.note: in here says one piece goes inside the other
don't start means the first letter of the word is dropped
topless means the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A warning against casual sex in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in here' looks like part of a scene-setting phrase but signals the container; the definition reads off the surface's 'this condition', meaning without sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sex, an organism reproducing by itself is not in a sexed condition.

clue.text: Mishit, of course, below the Athenaeum, say?

parts.note: the Athenaeum is a famous London gentlemen's club

explanation.surface: A bad golf shot lands beneath a London club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means on a golf course: to choose a club that is too weak for the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, choosing too little club makes the ball fall short, a mishit on the course.

clue.text: Perennial royal trophy

explanation.surface: A royal prize that keeps coming back every year.
explanation.walkthrough: Perennial is a plant here, not something recurring.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh marigold is a perennial plant flowering year after year.

clue.text: Exhibition of lightship switching

indicators.note: switching says the two halves of the word are taken in the opposite order

parts.note: the word splits into light (fair, pale in colour) and ship (craft, a vessel)
the light part means fair, pale in colour

explanation.surface: A display put on aboard a lightship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lightship' looks like a single vessel, but 'switching' asks you to split it and take its halves in the opposite order.
explanation.definitionFit: A show of handmade goods is an exhibition and sale.

clue.text: Try India's wretched cells

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Attempts at Indian prison cells prove miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' rearranges INDIA into NIDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonidia are the algal reproductive cells inside a lichen, a technical botanical term.

clue.text: Long distance call out?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as a cry from a distance, shouting out

explanation.surface: A phone call made over a great distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom normally means very different; the clue reads it literally twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom suggests a great distance, and literally a shout heard from afar.

clue.text: Mexican food causing end of fat East German woman

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: A Mexican snack made an overweight woman from East Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp fried tortilla with toppings is a Mexican dish.

clue.text: Out of which surprise, sadly, he gets into trouble, or quits

indicators.note: sadly means unhappily, so the pooled letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man unexpectedly lands in trouble and gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: HE joins TROUBLE, OR quits the pool, and 'sadly' rearranges what is left. The definition is the idiom: a surprise comes out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a sudden surprise is that something comes out of the sky, so the clear sky is what a surprise comes out of.

clue.text: The sweetener in a state of austerity? Me!

parts.note: Sparta was the ancient Greek state famous for austere living

explanation.surface: A diet sweetener claims to be the very picture of self-denial.
explanation.definitionFit: The artificial low-calorie compound is used as a sweetener in drinks.

clue.text: One in the eye for an unwilling school creeper?

definitions.meaning: the dark opening in the eye's iris
Shakespeare's schoolboy creeps like a snail unwillingly to school

explanation.surface: A setback for a boy reluctant to go to school.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense alludes to As You Like It: 'the whining schoolboy ... creeping like snail unwillingly to school'.
explanation.definitionFit: The schoolchild is a learner, and the eye has its dark centre of the same name.

clue.text: Old tax docked to pay tribute

indicators.note: docked means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a toll is a tax or charge

explanation.surface: A former tax, reduced, honours someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the last L from TOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise highly is to pay tribute to someone.

clue.text: Joint force

definitions.meaning: the joint in the middle of the arm
to push one's way, as in shoving through a crowd

explanation.surface: A cannabis joint used as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm's hinge joint, and as a verb to shove or barge aside.

clue.text: Flora's section of Singhalese palace

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Plant life in one part of a Sri Lankan palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf-like part of a flower's calyx is a part belonging to flora, plant life.

clue.text: Mass Observation director

parts.note: read as the person directing a celebration of Mass, rather than the head of the British social research project

explanation.surface: The head of a social research organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass Observation was a British social research project; here it means the officiant who leads the observance of Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The priest who officiates at the Eucharist leads, or directs, the observance of Mass.

clue.text: Establishment types putting Ken in Bloody Tower. 'e's not bothered!

indicators.note: bothered means flustered, so the letters are jumbled
not says the letter named is taken away
in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: 'e is he with the h dropped, standing for the letter E

explanation.surface: Insiders imprison Ken in the Tower of London, and he doesn't care.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bloody Tower is part of the Tower of London; the dropped-aitch 'e signals the letter to remove before 'bothered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal system of mutual help among former public school pupils is the preserve of Establishment types.
